newsitem.title: JAPAN: New Japan airline hopes to stir up competition.
newsitem.headline: New Japan airline hopes to stir up competition.

text.p: Japan's much-awaited discount airline says it hopes to create some competitive turbulence for the country's notoriously protected domestic airline industry.

Skymark Airlines Co Ltd, set up by leading Japanese discount airline ticket seller H.I.S Co Ltd, will offer services on one of the busiest domestic routes starting next summer, chairman Hideo Sawada said in a recent interview.

"We want to help bring about competition to stimulate the industry as a whole," Sawada told Reuters. "If possible we would like to make a profit in the first year of operation, although it is a big challenge,"
Sawada, also president of H.I.S, did not specify which route Skymark would start flying on, adding he wanted to be flexible about choosing a route.

Skymark was established by H.I.S. in November 1996 with the aim of offering cheap tickets to break into the domestic airline sector, which has often been criticised for its closely-guarded pricing system, especially by foreigners.
"This airline's top priorities are cheap prices, safety and good service," Sawada said.
"It is a challenge to cut air fares by 50 percent but costs can be kept low by rationalising, for example by using an efficient computer system in making reservations," he said.

Skymark, one of the first airline firms to enter the domestic aviation market in more than 40 years, is majority owned by H.I.S, which has a 58.7 percent stake. The other shareholders include Skymark president Junichi Ogawara, Orix Corp, Hikari Tsushin Inc and Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
Japan's heavily-regulated aviation industry was exposed to increased competition last year when the government allowed carriers more leeway in setting domestic fares.
Several other new domestic airlines have sprung up since then, but analysts said it was premature to judge whether the carriers posed an immediate threat to the established airlines.
Skymark will use H.I.S's marketing skills to attract consumers and will rely on Japan's top domestic carrier All Nippon Airways Co Ltd (ANA) for technical assistance, Sawada said.
Currently, giants ANA, Japan Airlines Co Ltd (JAL), and Japan Air System Co Ltd (JAS) dominate key domestic routes.

"What incumbent airlines are doing now is setting high prices on domestic routes, and using that profit to compete internationally. They will never achieve (international) competitiveness in the real sense under such an environment."
Sawada also said Skymark could eventually have tie-ups with foreign carriers.

"For instance, we could adopt code-sharing with a foreign carrier that flies to Fukuoka (in Kyushu in southern Japan), and allow passengers flying from there to Tokyo to make seat reservations at the point of departure," he said.
Sawada said competition from other new airlines was "a good sign."
"By having competition in service and prices among various new airlines, the good ones will remain," he said.
